subject: Electrical Engineering
title: Superconductors: Zero Resistance Dream
description: A quick win: understand Superconductors: Zero Resistance Dream.

hook.text: Cool certain materials below a critical temperature and resistance drops to zero.

buildup.text: Current flows forever in a superconducting loop — no heat, no loss at all.

discovery.text: MRI machines already use superconducting magnets cooled by liquid helium.

twist.text: The cooling costs more energy than the transmission savings — for now.

climax.text: Room-temperature superconductors would revolutionize the grid — if we ever find one.

punchline.text: Zero resistance is real — just not at room temperature yet.

quiz.question: Why aren't superconductors widely used in power grids yet?
options: They only work with DC current
The extreme cooling required costs more energy than the losses they prevent
Superconducting wire is too brittle to hang on towers
